translations.value: What should you do in the following scenarios?

The red marks located in this warehouse will take you to different scenarios. When you click on a red marker, a situation will be described and you will have to answer a question. After answering the question you will receive an explanation as to what the correct answer is. Every time you answer a question correctly you will get a star.

It's incredibly busy. You'll be working with the forklift for a few hours to get everything in the right place. You're a bit worried. 
The forklift you're working with suddenly makes a strange noise when the forks are in their highest position. What do you do?
https://21cccdn.blob.core.windows.net/21cc/games/images/vcaWarehouse/scenarios/broken-forklift/broken-forklift-description-mainfreight.jpg
1. You just carry on as usual for now. Aside from the strange noise, the forklift is still working fine.
2. You stop it and leave it there. You immediately notify your supervisor and place signage around the forklift.
3. You turn it off and try to solve the problem yourself.
4. You stop it, lower your load and call the technical service.

The most important rule to follow if you suspect something is wrong with your forklift, or any other piece of equipment, is to stop as quickly as possible and ensure it doesn't pose a danger to yourself or others.

In this case, you must immediately stop the forklift and lower the load. If you're unable to lower the load, you must cordon off the area around the forklift with tape, for example, to indicate the dangerous situation. Then, inform your team leader and, if necessary, the technical department to report the problem and learn what to do next.

You should not continue driving if something is potentially wrong. This can be dangerous for you and your colleagues. Trying to fix it or repair it yourself is not recommended. Often, only certified technicians are allowed to carry out repairs. Leaving the forklift alone with the load raised without cordoning off the area with tape is unsafe.

You've just started work. It's luckily never happened to you before, but you just rear-ended your forklift against some shelving. Luckily, you only hit it lightly. You get out to check if the shelving and/or the forklift are damaged. You see absolutely nothing. Nothing is bent, dented, scratched, or anything. Phew, that's lucky! What do you do?
https://21cccdn.blob.core.windows.net/21cc/games/images/vcaWarehouse/scenarios/forklift-crash/forklift-crash-description-mainfreight.jpg
1. You've done a thorough inspection. Nothing is broken. There's no reason to report it and bother anyone with it.
2. You immediately report it to your manager.
3. You report it to your manager at the end of your shift.

If something like this happens to you, you're naturally not proud of it. But always report it immediately. This could prevent much more serious accidents for yourself or your colleagues.Even invisible damage to scaffolding can cause the whole thing to collapse, with all the consequences that entails.

You work in a warehouse where the lighting in one aisle is poor. For example, you can only read your order picking form if you use your mobile phone's flashlight for additional illumination. This aisle also has a visitor path. Luckily, you've never hit anyone with your forklift. What would you do in such a situation?

Report dangerous situations immediately to your supervisor or the prevention officer. Poor visibility is very dangerous. The risk of collisions with pedestrians and crossing traffic is therefore significantly increased. And using your mobile phone (or having to use it) while driving a forklift is a no-go! 

Of course, it's good to drive carefully, but if you never report a situation you consider dangerous, nothing will likely change. Do not report dangerous situations directly to the inspectorate (the full name is: Inspection Service of the Ministry of Social Affairs and Employment). Only when it proves impossible to resolve the problems within the organization through reasonable consultation should you decide to report them to the inspectorate.
https://21cccdn.blob.core.windows.net/21cc/games/images/vcaWarehouse/scenarios/dark-warehouse/dark-warehouse-description-mainfreight.png
1. You report this to your team leader.
2. You report this to the prevention officer.
3. You try to drive as calmly as possible in those areas.
4. You report this to the Inspectorate (I-SZW).

The dock leveler at one of the loading bays where trucks can load and unload is in poor condition. The wheels of the roll containers coming out of the trucks often get stuck in the gap that has formed. You then have to push and pull quite hard to get the roll containers across. What do you do?
https://21cccdn.blob.core.windows.net/21cc/games/images/vcaWarehouse/scenarios/loading-dock/loading-dock-mainfreight-description.jpg
1. You report this to your team leader.
2. You report it to the prevention officer.
3. You place planks over the cracks and holes.
4. You ask a colleague to help you.

You need to report this for several reasons. It slows down the loading and unloading process, it's unpleasant and physically demanding for you (health), and it's simply dangerous (safety). What if you have to pull or push so hard that a cart tips over? Although well-intentioned, it's usually not the goal for you to carry out repairs yourself or come up with temporary fixes. Perhaps another loading platform can be used until this one is repaired.
